title: Amar Nath Vidya Ashram & Anr. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Anjani Kumar Mishra, J. and Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; relegated to CGRF/Ombudsman under clause 7.10, to be decided preferably within three months
headnote: A remaining technical billing dispute after the consumer has deposited the impugned demand — here, a multiplication-factor change from 1 to 4 following amalgamation of three connections into one, and a claim to bifurcate mixed commercial and staff-quarter (domestic) load on that connection — is for the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum / Ombudsman under paragraph 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, not the writ court. The petitioners, challenging a demand notice dated 18.10.2017, were left free to file a complaint before that forum, to be considered and decided expeditiously, preferably within three months of filing a certified copy of the order with the complaint. The writ was disposed of subject to that liberty. The Court did not decide the quantum of the demand, the multiplication-factor change, or the mixed-use bifurcation.
facts:
The petitioners, Amar Nath Vidya Ashram and another, challenged a demand notice dated 18 October 2017. The institution originally held three connections (S.C. Nos. 007641, 068315 and 047169). After an inspection they were directed to amalgamate those connections; a single connection was issued, but the multiplication factor was then changed from 1 to 4, producing a dispute over the amount payable. They also said the same connection supplied both the institution and staff quarters, mixing commercial and domestic use.

They were told to deposit the demanded sum first; they claimed they had paid it, including Rs 20 lakh on 5 and 6 March 2018 as stated at the 19 March 2018 listing, but that the licensee had not bifurcated the commercial and residential components. On 19 March 2018 the Court directed that if that deposit was made, the connection would not be disconnected till the next date.

holding_units.topic: Post-deposit technical billing dispute (MF change on amalgamation; mixed commercial/domestic load) belongs to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman
holding_units.question: After the consumer has deposited the impugned demand, should the writ court decide a remaining technical billing dispute about a multiplication-factor change on amalgamation of connections and mixed commercial/domestic use, or is that for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman?
holding_units.holding: It is for the Clause 7.10 forum. After deposit of the amount claimed in the demand notice dated 18.10.2017, the remaining issue is a technical one best addressed by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum / Ombudsman under paragraph 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner may file a complaint before that forum, which shall consider and decide it expeditiously, preferably within three months from the date a certified copy of the order is filed with the complaint. Subject to that, the writ petition stands disposed of.
holding_units.flag: Source PDF also contains listing orders of 19.3.2018 (interim non-disconnection if the stated Rs 20 lakh deposit was made), 13.3.2024, 22.4.2024 and 15.1.2025; the operative disposal is 7.2.2025.

principle_tags.application: A remaining technical billing grievance after deposit of the demand (multiplication-factor change on amalgamation of three connections; mixed commercial/domestic load on the single connection) is for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman in the first instance, not the writ court. Same cluster as SCJ-096, SCJ-197, SCJ-217.

not_decided.point: Correctness / quantum of the demand notice dated 18.10.2017, including whether the multiplication factor was rightly changed from 1 to 4 after amalgamation
not_decided.note: Left to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman; the Court expressed no opinion on the amount chargeable.

not_decided.point: Whether the single connection should be bifurcated into commercial and residential (staff-quarter) components
not_decided.note: Raised as the remaining grievance after deposit; expressly treated as a technical issue for the CGRF/Ombudsman.
